basis: Omnisciente assessment guidance, checked against CIS v8.1 safeguard descriptions. Evidence examples are alternatives, not additional requirements. CAS scoring, inputs and metrics are not imported.

review: Compare the inventory with the devices actually used: endpoints (including portable and mobile), servers, network equipment and data-capable IoT/non-computing devices. Include physical, virtual, remote and cloud assets, plus regularly connected assets outside the organization's control.

Confirm each entry records its static network address when applicable, hardware address, machine name, owner, department and approval to connect. Look for missing devices, duplicate entries and retired devices still shown as active.
Check dated inventory reviews and updates occur at least every six months. Discovery and device-management tools can help reconcile coverage; a particular tool is not required.
evidence: An asset inventory export with the specified identifying fields.
Dated reconciliation notes compared with network, endpoint or responsible-provider records.
outcome: The inventory accounts for the full asset population and identifies who owns each device and whether it may connect.
Inventory changes and reviews demonstrate currency within the six-month interval.

review: Review how unknown or unauthorized devices are identified and handled each week. Compare recent inventory differences or network observations with the handling records.

Confirm unauthorized devices are removed from the network, denied remote connection or quarantined. Identify devices that remain connected without authorization; an open remediation ticket alone does not resolve them.
evidence: Weekly unauthorized-device review records or provider reports showing the devices examined.
Dated removal, connection-denial or quarantine results matched to the identified devices.
outcome: Weekly handling operates, and unauthorized devices do not retain unaddressed network access.
Records demonstrate the disposition of identified devices, not only their discovery.

review: Configure discovery coverage and accountable operator. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Run discovery and reconcile unexpected devices. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Daily or more often. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Discovery run and reconciliation records. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Discover connected devices automatically. Run discovery and reconcile unexpected devices.
Daily or more often. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Identify every DHCP server or the IP address management tools and compare their log coverage with the inventory. Confirm the logs are reviewed and used for inventory updates at least weekly.
Collect observations and resolve inventory differences. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
At least weekly inventory updates using logs. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Dated reconciliation and source coverage. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Feed address-allocation observations into inventory. Collect observations and resolve inventory differences.
At least weekly inventory updates using logs. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: [Requirement check 1.5] Were passive-discovery results reviewed and used to update inventory at least weekly? [Explanatory prompt] Which networks or weeks lack supporting records?

Confirm monitored network segments and reconcile dated discoveries to inventory entries. Trace an unknown asset through ownership and authorization decisions; check gaps between weekly reconciliations.

Scope and timing: At least weekly: review discovery results and use them to update inventory. Passive discovery operates between those reviews. Use dated operational records; completing this governance Review does not itself demonstrate technical execution.
evidence: Sensor coverage map, discovery output, dated inventory change log or provider reconciliation record.
Relevant existing records or equivalent support may be linked; these examples are not mandatory files.
outcome: Discover connected assets passively; use the results to refresh the asset inventory at least weekly. At least weekly: review discovery results and use them to update inventory. Passive discovery operates between those reviews.
Coverage, exceptions and unresolved gaps are accurately recorded, with implementation and verification assessed separately.

review: Review the inventory of licensed software installed on enterprise assets. Confirm each entry has a title, publisher, initial installation/use date and business purpose.

Check URL, app store, versions, deployment mechanism, retirement date and license count where appropriate. Compare recorded software with installed applications and operating systems to find omissions.
Verify the inventory is reviewed and updated at least every six months. Automated inventory tools are an option, not an IG1 prerequisite.
evidence: Software inventory or application catalog containing the relevant fields.
Dated reconciliation with installed-software reports, licensing records or provider-maintained inventories.
outcome: Installed software can be identified and connected to a documented business purpose.
The inventory has the specified details and a current six-month review/update record.

review: Compare authorized software versions against publisher support information at least monthly. Identify end-of-support products incorrectly marked as supported.

For necessary mission-supporting software that is unsupported, examine a documented exception covering mitigating controls and acceptance of residual risk. Without that exception, confirm it is classified as unauthorized.
evidence: Version inventory matched to publisher lifecycle notices and dated monthly support checks.
For necessary unsupported software, its exception and evidence that the stated mitigation operates.
outcome: Authorization reflects current vendor support or the safeguard's documented exception conditions.
Unsupported software is not silently treated as supported; monthly checks identify changes.

review: Compare installed software with the authorized inventory and examine the disposition of unapproved installations.
Confirm unauthorized software is removed from use or has a documented exception, with review at least monthly. Pending investigation or a planned removal is not completed handling.
evidence: Monthly software reconciliation or provider review identifying unauthorized installations.
Removal results or documented exceptions tied to the software and affected assets.
outcome: Unauthorized installations have a demonstrated removal or a documented exception.
Monthly reviews can account for software that was discovered and what happened to it.

review: Choose coverage and document technical limitations. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain discovery coverage and inventory feed. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Tool coverage and inventory samples. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Automate installed-software visibility where possible. Maintain discovery coverage and inventory feed.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Define approved software and exception handling. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Enforce application restrictions. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Reassess at least every six months. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Policy configuration, exception and reassessment records. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Restrict execution/access to approved applications. Enforce application restrictions.
Reassess at least every six months. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Define authorized libraries and deployment limitations. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Enforce library controls; handle changes safely. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Reassess at least every six months. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Library rule samples and reassessment results. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Prevent unapproved libraries loading. Enforce library controls; handle changes safely.
Reassess at least every six months. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: [Requirement check 2.7] Does technical enforcement allow authorized scripts and block unauthorized scripts, and was it reassessed within six months? [Explanatory prompt] Which execution paths were examined?

Identify script execution paths, including administrative tools, email and browser handling. Confirm authorized execution and blocked unauthorized execution using safe existing test results; check the latest reassessment date.

Scope and timing: CIS says bi-annually or more frequently. Interpret as every six months, supported by the CAS six-month test; enforcement is ongoing. Use dated operational records; completing this governance Review does not itself demonstrate technical execution.
evidence: Approved script list, enforcement configuration, safe allow/block test results, reassessment record.
Relevant existing records or equivalent support may be linked; these examples are not mandatory files.
outcome: Enforce execution of authorized scripts only and block others; reassess at least every six months. CIS says bi-annually or more frequently. Interpret as every six months, supported by the CAS six-month test; enforcement is ongoing.
Coverage, exceptions and unresolved gaps are accurately recorded, with implementation and verification assessed separately.

review: Review the documented data-management process for sensitivity, ownership, handling, retention limits and disposal requirements.
Confirm these expectations reflect the organization's sensitivity and retention standards. Check review/update dates annually and after significant changes affecting the process.
evidence: Data-management procedures or standards addressing the required subjects.
Revision records or dated reviews explaining updates after relevant changes.
outcome: People responsible for data can determine its handling, retention and disposal requirements.
Documentation reflects current operations and receives annual and significant-change review.

review: Compare the data inventory with the documented data-management process. Confirm sensitive data is included at a minimum, rather than inventorying systems alone.
Review relevant repositories and business processes for omitted data. Verify inventory reviews and updates at least annually, prioritizing sensitive information.
evidence: Data inventory linked to the systems or locations holding the identified data.
Dated annual reconciliation with data owners or responsible providers.
outcome: The organization can identify its sensitive data and account for it in the inventory.
The inventory follows the data-management process and has been reviewed within the annual interval.

review: Inspect access permissions for local and remote file systems, databases and applications. Compare access with users' need to know.
Identify broad groups, inherited permissions and unnecessary access that expose data beyond business need. An access policy alone does not demonstrate the configured permissions.
evidence: Permission exports or configuration views from the relevant repositories.
Business-role information or access-review records explaining why the observed access is needed.
outcome: Effective permissions restrict access according to business need across the relevant data locations.
The observed configuration agrees with the stated access model.

review: Review the documented minimum and maximum retention periods for the relevant data.
Compare retention settings and actual retained data with those periods. Identify premature deletion and data kept beyond its maximum period; a written schedule alone is insufficient.
evidence: Retention requirements together with repository or system retention settings.
Dated retention/deletion results or provider records showing how the periods are enforced.
outcome: Data is retained for the required minimum period and not kept beyond the documented maximum.
Actual retention behavior matches the organization's data-management process.

review: Review disposal procedures and recent disposal activity for electronic and physical data.
Confirm the method matches data sensitivity and the documented data-management process. Check that a request to dispose was actually carried out.
evidence: Disposal procedure and dated deletion, sanitization or destruction records.
Provider disposal certificates or execution reports identifying the affected data or media.
outcome: Disposal follows the documented process using a method suited to the sensitivity involved.
Completed disposal can be distinguished from work merely scheduled or requested.

review: Identify end-user devices containing sensitive data, including portable and mobile devices, and inspect their encryption state.
Compare the device population with encryption results to find missing or disabled protection. Product selection is optional; encryption of the sensitive data is the requirement.
evidence: Encryption-state reports or device configuration views matched to the sensitive-data device population.
Client or provider verification of actual encryption coverage, excluding passwords and recovery keys.
outcome: Sensitive data on end-user devices is encrypted.
The claim is supported by device-level state, not only an intended encryption policy.

review: Agree classification criteria with data owners. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Apply classification in handling decisions. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Annual review and significant-change updates. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Classification scheme and owner decisions. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Give information consistent sensitivity classifications. Apply classification in handling decisions.
Annual review and significant-change updates. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Compare documented internal and service-provider data flows with the enterprise data management process. Confirm annual updates and updates after significant changes affecting those flows.
Maintain flows through service changes. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Annual review and significant-change updates. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Flow diagrams or equivalent controlled records. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Make internal and provider data movements traceable. Maintain flows through service changes.
Annual review and significant-change updates. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Define permitted media and encryption arrangements. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Enforce media encryption. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Configuration sample and coverage exceptions. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Protect removable-media contents with encryption. Enforce media encryption.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Identify sensitive flows and protected transports. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain encrypted transport. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Transport configurations and sampled connection results. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Protect sensitive information during transfer. Maintain encrypted transport.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Identify storage and encryption coverage; storage-layer protection suffices for the stated minimum. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain encryption coverage. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Storage encryption settings and scoped assurance. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Protect stored sensitive server/application/database information. Maintain encryption coverage.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Define sensitivity boundaries and permitted processing locations. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Enforce storage and processing separation. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Architecture and boundary configuration samples. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Keep sensitive processing out of lower-trust environments. Enforce storage and processing separation.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: [Requirement check 3.13] Does automated discovery cover sensitive data across the stated locations and feed the inventory? [Explanatory prompt] Show a recent detected location and its inventory entry.
Confirm coverage of stored, processed and transmitted sensitive information, including remote-provider locations. Trace a detected data location to the inventory and investigate blind spots.

Scope and timing: No fixed interval specified. The automated capability and inventory-update process must operate. Use dated operational records; completing this governance Review does not itself demonstrate technical execution.
evidence: Discovery coverage/export, DLP configuration, provider coverage statement and matched data-inventory update.
Relevant existing records or equivalent support may be linked; these examples are not mandatory files.
outcome: Use automated sensitive-data discovery across enterprise and provider assets, and update the data inventory. No fixed interval specified. The automated capability and inventory-update process must operate.
Coverage, exceptions and unresolved gaps are accurately recorded, with implementation and verification assessed separately.

review: [Requirement check 3.14] Are sensitive-data access, modification and disposal recorded? [Explanatory prompt] Which data stores and event types do the examples cover?
Compare sensitive-data locations to enabled audit sources. Inspect representative access, modification and deletion records and identify locations or event types that are not recorded.

Scope and timing: No fixed review interval specified. Logging must cover relevant access events as they occur. Use dated operational records; completing this governance Review does not itself demonstrate technical execution.
evidence: Audit-source configuration and representative access, change and disposal log entries.
Relevant existing records or equivalent support may be linked; these examples are not mandatory files.
outcome: Record access to sensitive data, including changes and disposal. No fixed review interval specified. Logging must cover relevant access events as they occur.
Coverage, exceptions and unresolved gaps are accurately recorded, with implementation and verification assessed separately.

review: Review the documented secure-configuration process for endpoints, portable/mobile devices, IoT/non-computing assets, servers, operating systems and applications.
Confirm the process covers the technologies actually used. Check annual documentation reviews and updates following significant changes that affect configuration.
evidence: Configuration procedures and relevant baseline examples.
Dated process reviews and change records showing that documentation remains current.
outcome: There is a documented way to establish and maintain secure configurations across the asset and software scope.
The process is reviewed annually and when significant changes affect it.

review: Review the documented secure-configuration process specifically for network devices, such as routers, switches, firewalls and wireless infrastructure.
Compare the process with the current network estate. Verify annual review/update and review after significant changes affecting the safeguard.
evidence: Network configuration procedures or standards, with relevant device baselines.
Annual review records and revisions resulting from network changes.
outcome: Network infrastructure is covered by a maintained configuration process, not just endpoint guidance.
Documentation keeps pace with annual review and significant network changes.

review: Inspect applied inactivity-lock settings and confirm sessions lock automatically within 15 minutes on general-purpose operating systems and within 2 minutes on mobile end-user devices.
Compare assigned policies with effective device settings or observed behavior. Look for exclusions or overrides that leave sessions unlocked.
evidence: Effective session-lock settings or policy-deployment reports by device type.
A safe observation of automatic locking on representative devices.
outcome: Sessions lock automatically within the applicable 15-minute or 2-minute limit.
The limits operate on devices rather than existing only in a proposed policy.

review: Identify servers that support a firewall and inspect whether firewall protection is implemented and managed.
Check for disabled protection or servers missed by the selected solution. An operating-system firewall, virtual firewall or third-party agent can be used; no named product is required.
evidence: Server inventory compared with firewall coverage and effective configuration.
Management or provider records showing the deployed firewall state.
outcome: Servers have managed firewall protection wherever supported.
Coverage and active settings substantiate the implementation claim.

review: Inspect host firewall or port-filtering settings on end-user devices, including laptops used away from the office.
Confirm the effective default is to deny traffic, with only explicitly allowed services and ports permitted. Look for disabled profiles and broad rules that undermine that default.
evidence: Effective endpoint firewall rules and deployment/coverage reports.
Configuration observations or provider reports confirming the policy operates on devices.
outcome: End-user devices apply default-deny filtering with explicit permitted services and ports.
Protection remains active in the device's relevant network profiles.

review: Review how assets and software are administered, including the protocols used to reach management interfaces.

Confirm secure management methods are used. Identify insecure protocols such as Telnet or HTTP and verify any continued use is operationally essential, not merely convenient. Infrastructure-as-Code is an example, not mandatory.
evidence: Administrative-interface settings, connection configurations or management procedures.
Change records or provider demonstrations showing secure administration in use and any operationally essential exception.
outcome: Administration uses secure methods appropriate to the assets and software.
Insecure management protocols are absent unless the safeguard's operational-necessity condition applies.

review: Identify vendor-preconfigured accounts on assets and software, including administrator and root accounts, and inspect how they are managed.
Confirm the selected treatment is applied. Disabling or making such accounts unusable are examples; do not assume merely renaming an account establishes secure management.
evidence: Default-account configuration or account-state records for relevant systems.
Provisioning or provider records showing the treatment applied to preconfigured accounts.
outcome: Default accounts are deliberately managed rather than left in an unmanaged installation state.
Observed account settings agree with the organization's chosen treatment.

review: Identify required services and approved baselines. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Remove or disable unnecessary services. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Baseline and sampled service inventory. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Remove unnecessary exposed functionality. Remove or disable unnecessary services.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Agree approved DNS resolvers for network infrastructure. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain trusted resolver settings. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Network configuration samples. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Use trustworthy infrastructure name resolution. Maintain trusted resolver settings.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Define lockout configuration by device class. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Enforce lockout thresholds. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Where supported: at most 20 failed attempts on laptops; 10 on tablets/phones. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Device policy and representative test result. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Limit repeated local authentication failures on portable devices. Enforce lockout thresholds.
Where supported: at most 20 failed attempts on laptops; 10 on tablets/phones. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Establish authorized wipe process for enterprise-owned portable devices. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain capability; execute on approved events. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Event: loss, theft or end of engagement are examples; no fixed interval. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Capability coverage and authorized wipe record. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Remove enterprise data remotely when appropriate. Maintain capability; execute on approved events.
Event: loss, theft or end of engagement are examples; no fixed interval. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: [Requirement check 4.12] Do supported mobile devices separate enterprise and personal workspaces? [Explanatory prompt] Which devices cannot support separation and how was that established?

Establish the supported mobile population, examine assigned profiles and confirm enterprise applications/data are separated from personal use. Record unsupported-device conditions without treating the whole safeguard as excluded.

Scope and timing: No fixed interval specified; maintain the separation on supported devices. Use dated operational records; completing this governance Review does not itself demonstrate technical execution.
evidence: Device capability inventory, management-profile configuration, representative device compliance record.
Relevant existing records or equivalent support may be linked; these examples are not mandatory files.
outcome: Separate enterprise and personal workspaces on mobile devices wherever supported. No fixed interval specified; maintain the separation on supported devices.
Coverage, exceptions and unresolved gaps are accurately recorded, with implementation and verification assessed separately.

review: Compare the account inventory with directories, applications and platforms, including user, administrator and service accounts.
Confirm records contain the person's name, username, start/stop dates and department. Identify active accounts missing from the inventory or lacking authorization.
Verify active-account authorization is validated at least quarterly; collecting an export alone is not an authorization review.
evidence: Account inventory and account/role exports from the client or responsible provider.
Dated quarterly authorization decisions tied to the reviewed accounts.
outcome: Accounts are identifiable in the inventory with the specified details.
Active-account authorization is demonstrated by recurring quarterly or more frequent validation.

review: Review password-setting and credential-management practices to confirm passwords are unique across enterprise assets. Do not request actual passwords to prove this.
CIS gives best-practice examples of at least 8 characters with MFA and 14 without MFA. Compare those examples with the organization's approach without treating them as a new Omnisciente scoring rule.
evidence: Password-policy configuration and credential-handling procedures without secret values.
A responsible-party demonstration or explanation of how reuse across assets is avoided; settings alone may not prove uniqueness.
outcome: Passwords are not reused across enterprise assets.
The assessment explains the basis for that conclusion without collecting credentials.

review: Review account-activity data and the handling of accounts inactive for 45 days. Confirm they are disabled or deleted where supported.
Compare inactivity dates with actual disablement/deletion results. A monthly evidence-review meeting must not extend the 45-day threshold; a generic risk acceptance is not a substitute.
evidence: Account inactivity reports and dated account-state changes.
Client or provider execution records confirming which dormant accounts were disabled or deleted.
outcome: Dormant accounts are disabled or removed after the 45-day inactivity period where the system supports it.
The record demonstrates the action, not only identification of inactivity.

review: Compare privileged-role assignments with the accounts used for ordinary work. Confirm administrator privileges are restricted to dedicated administrative accounts.
Check that web browsing, email and productivity work use the person's primary nonprivileged account. Look for everyday accounts retaining administrator privileges.
evidence: Privileged-account and role listings alongside ordinary user-account records.
Access procedures or representative activity records showing separation in practice.
outcome: Dedicated accounts perform administration; routine computing uses nonprivileged accounts.
Actual role assignments support that separation.

review: Identify service accounts, department owners, purpose and review dates. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain inventory through account changes. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Authorization review at least quarterly. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
Check the following aspects: Service-account records identify the responsible department, owner, purpose and review date; authorization reviews occur at least quarterly.
evidence: Service-account register and authorization decisions. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Keep service-account purpose and ownership accountable. Maintain inventory through account changes.
Authorization review at least quarterly. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Identify directory/identity authority and exceptions. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Operate centralized account management. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Directory coverage and exception records. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Consolidate account administration. Operate centralized account management.
No numeric interval specified. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Review the documented access-granting process for new hires and role changes.

Compare recent hires or changes with resulting access to confirm the process is followed. Automation is preferred in the safeguard, not a prerequisite or a requirement for a particular approval chain.
evidence: Access-granting procedure and relevant hire/role-change requests.
Provisioning records or responsible-provider results showing the resulting access.
outcome: A documented granting process operates for both new hires and changed roles.
Access decisions and resulting provisioning can be followed through actual examples.

review: Review the revocation process and compare termination, rights-revocation and role-change times with account disablement.

Confirm access is disabled immediately when those events require revocation. A later periodic review does not replace immediate action. Disabling rather than deleting may be needed to preserve audit trails.
evidence: Offboarding/role-change records compared with timestamped disablement logs.
Revocation procedure and provider execution records where access is externally managed.
outcome: Required revocation takes effect immediately, rather than waiting for the next scheduled review.
The organization can demonstrate when access was disabled and retain necessary attribution.

review: Identify externally exposed enterprise and third-party applications. Inspect whether MFA is enforced wherever supported, rather than merely available for enrollment.
Check direct sign-in and SSO routes for bypasses. Enforcement through a directory or SSO provider is acceptable; note actual support limitations separately from incomplete deployment.
evidence: Application/sign-in inventory and MFA or conditional-access configuration.
Authentication results or provider records demonstrating enforced MFA on applicable routes.
outcome: Externally exposed applications enforce MFA wherever they support it.
Alternative access paths do not silently bypass the intended enforcement.

review: Review all remote network-access methods and confirm MFA is required for connections.
Inspect applied authentication policies and representative connection results. Identify alternate remote-access paths that still permit a password alone.
evidence: Remote-access configurations and authentication policies.
Connection/authentication logs or a safe sign-in demonstration from the client or provider.
outcome: Remote network access requires MFA.
The implemented connection behavior matches the configuration claim.

review: Review administrative accounts across enterprise assets, including on-site and service-provider-managed environments.
Confirm MFA is enforced for administrative access wherever supported. Identify excluded accounts, alternative admin interfaces and enrollment without enforcement.
evidence: Administrative-account lists matched to effective MFA policies.
Admin sign-in results or scoped provider evidence confirming enforcement.
outcome: Administrative access requires MFA wherever supported, including provider-managed assets.
Coverage is demonstrated for the administrative population, not inferred from ordinary-user MFA.

review: Inventory internal and provider-hosted identity systems. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Maintain system inventory. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
Review/update at least annually. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: Identity-system register and reviewed changes. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Identify all authentication/authorization systems. Maintain system inventory.
Review/update at least annually. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: Define directory/SSO coverage and limitations. Confirm the covered population and client decisions.
Operate centralized access control. Check actual execution rather than a policy statement alone.
No numeric interval specified; where supported. Confirm relevant exceptions and follow-up with the accountable owner.
evidence: SSO coverage and access configuration samples. Use representative records covering the stated population.
Existing Reviews, Findings and Actions can trace exceptions and validation; combined records may support multiple safeguards.
outcome: Consolidate supported access enforcement. Operate centralized access control.
No numeric interval specified; where supported. Retain a clear account of scope, operating responsibility and unresolved gaps.

review: [Requirement check 6.8] Are role rights documented and all asset privileges validated as authorized at least annually? [Explanatory prompt] Does the existing quarterly account review cover privileges as well as account existence?

Compare job duties, role definitions and actual asset privileges. Confirm reviews cover all privileges, including privileged and service access where relevant; investigate excessive and unmapped rights.

Scope and timing: Access-control review at least annually or more often. Role definitions and rights are maintained. Use dated operational records; completing this governance Review does not itself demonstrate technical execution.
evidence: Role-to-rights matrix, entitlement export, dated authorization review and resulting corrections.
Relevant existing records or equivalent support may be linked; these examples are not mandatory files.
outcome: Document necessary rights by role; review asset privileges for authorization at least annually. Access-control review at least annually or more often. Role definitions and rights are maintained.
Coverage, exceptions and unresolved gaps are accurately recorded, with implementation and verification assessed separately.

review: Review the documented vulnerability-management process and its coverage of enterprise assets.
Confirm the process reflects current operations and is reviewed/updated annually and after significant changes. Do not import IG2 scanning frequencies into this IG1 process requirement.
evidence: Vulnerability-management procedures and their asset scope.
Dated reviews or revisions showing annual and significant-change maintenance.
outcome: A current, documented process governs vulnerability management for enterprise assets.
Relevant changes and annual reviews keep the process usable.

review: Review the documented remediation process and how its strategy prioritizes work by risk.
Confirm monthly or more frequent process reviews. Examine remediation records to understand how prioritization operates; the safeguard does not impose one universal deadline for every vulnerability.
evidence: Risk-based remediation procedure and prioritization criteria.
Dated monthly reviews supported by remediation queues, decisions or provider reports.
outcome: Risk drives a documented remediation strategy.
Monthly or more frequent reviews evaluate the process; unresolved work is not mistaken for completed remediation.

review: Compare operating-system patch schedules and deployment results with the enterprise asset population.

Confirm automated patch management actually applies OS updates monthly or more frequently. Identify failed, missed and incomplete deployments; a monthly report or accepted delay is not equivalent to applying updates.
evidence: Automated patch configuration and dated OS deployment results.
Asset-level update status or provider execution reports, including failed jobs and subsequent outcomes.
outcome: OS updates are applied through automated patch management at least monthly.
Results substantiate deployment across the asset population, not only the existence of a schedule.
